cohort: 102 pregnant women, 51 with preeclampsia and 51 normotensive nonproteinuric controls, excluding those who smoked, consumed alcohol, had multiple gestation, diabetes mellitus, or renal failure.
finding: Women with preeclampsia had significantly higher serum uric acid levels compared to controls, and higher uric acid levels were associated with severe preeclampsia and poorer perinatal outcomes (lower APGAR scores and birth weight).
birth_weight: Lower birth weight was observed in women with elevated serum uric acid levels.
